findings.subject: search-field
findings.summary: SearchField drops a consumer ref and silently ignores size and invalid.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/search-field/search-field.tsx:97-102 spreads props (type includes ref) then overrides ref={inputRef}; size goes only to the unstyled InputGroupInput while chrome height comes from InputGroup data-size (input-group.tsx:73) and size rules exclude [data-unstyled] (input.css:229-251).
findings.fix: Merge the consumer ref with inputRef (callback ref), pass size and invalid to InputGroup instead of the inner input, and add tests for ref, size and invalid.

verified.reason: search-field.tsx spreads {...props} into InputGroupInput, then sets ref={inputRef} after it. On React 19 the consumer's ref is an ordinary prop, so it gets replaced. size and invalid also reach only the unstyled inner Input. InputGroup gets neither: it renders data-size from its own default (md) and no data-invalid. The sm/lg rules in input.css exclude [data-unstyled]. The invalid rule on the inner span only sets custom properties, but the group draws the border from its own properties. So the size and invalid chrome never change, which breaks the K1 rule that props match the contract and refs are forwarded.

findings.subject: field
findings.summary: Field never associates its description or error with the control, and its own Playground example ships an unassociated description.
findings.evidence: field.tsx:89-169 (no ids, no context); field.stories.tsx:31-35; field.json crossRenderer accessibilityOutcomes associates-description, announces-error, parity strict.
findings.fix: Give Field a context with generated ids: FieldLabel htmlFor, FieldDescription/FieldError ids, and expose them (or wrap Base UI Field) so the control gets aria-describedby and aria-invalid; fix the Playground and add an association test.

verified.reason: Field, FieldDescription and FieldError in field.tsx create no ids, no context and no aria-describedby. Only form.tsx (FormControl) wires association. The Field Playground story renders FieldDescription with no aria-describedby on the Input. field.json lists associates-description in accessibilityOutcomes, with parity strict and a React adaptation that says it uses DOM description relationships. FieldError's role=alert covers part of announces-error, but the description outcome is unmet.

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: Select has no invalid state, and its open popup states are never baselined.
findings.evidence: select.json states omit invalid; select.css has 0 invalid rules; form.tsx:114 sets aria-invalid on the trigger with no visual; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-select-grouped-chromium-linux.png and -scrollable- show only the closed trigger.
findings.fix: Add 'invalid' to the contract and style [aria-invalid='true'],[data-invalid] like .a63-Input[data-invalid]; open the Grouped/Scrollable stories (defaultOpen or a play function) so the popup, highlighted and selected items are captured.

verified.reason: select.json states (closed, open, placeholder, focus-visible, disabled, highlighted-item, selected-item, disabled-item) include no invalid state, and select.css has no invalid or aria-invalid rule. FormControl sets aria-invalid on the trigger, but the only visual is the text color Field[data-invalid] passes down, with no danger edge on the trigger. The grouped baseline shows only the closed trigger. No story opens the popup, so the required open state is never captured.

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: Select carries five documented APG keyboard gaps from Base UI 1.6.0 (Tab does not select, Home/End do not open, Alt+Up does not select, no aria-activedescendant).
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/select.json contract.accessibility.knownGaps; docs/design-system/audits/base-ui-issue-drafts.md.
findings.fix: File the drafted Base UI issues; patch Tab-selects locally with an onKeyDown on the popup if Base UI does not move.

findings.subject: input, select, autocomplete, search-field, input-otp
findings.summary: Text fields, select triggers and OTP slots are 32px tall on coarse pointers with no 44px target, against the system's own rule.
findings.evidence: environment.css:51-62,128-136 ('Recipes must ... expand the touch region with min-target'); button.css:130-136 does it; input.css, select.css, autocomplete.css, input-otp.css never reference --a63-control-min-target.
findings.fix: Floor field heights with --a63-control-min-target on coarse pointers, or add the ::before target used by Button; extend check:control-alignment to assert target size on touch.

findings.subject: input, textarea, input-otp, search-field
findings.summary: Focus-visible and hover are styled but never captured in a baseline; the OTP active slot is never shown.
findings.evidence: No play function in input/textarea/input-otp/search-field stories (grep 'play:' finds none); ui-react-input-states-chromium-linux.png shows rest/filled/invalid/disabled only; ui-react-inputotp-themes shows no active slot.
findings.fix: Add a Focused story per component with a play function that focuses the field, captured in the visual suite.

findings.subject: input, textarea, input-otp, search-field, autocomplete, select
findings.summary: No phone-width story for any text or choice field.
findings.evidence: Batch screenshots include only amount-phone-balance at phone form factor; the 16px font floor is covered by recipes.test.ts:309-314.
findings.fix: Add one phone story per field type (AppView layout="phone", touch input) to the visual suite.

findings.subject: field
findings.summary: Field's invalid and disabled states are raw data-* strings, repeated on the control, instead of props.
findings.evidence: field.css:75,153; field.stories.tsx:44-46.
findings.fix: Add invalid and disabled props to Field that set the attributes and flow to the control through context, as InputGroup does (input-group.tsx:17-27).

findings.subject: field
findings.summary: Field guidance says to wire ARIA relationships, but the documented example does not.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component field` Guidance bullet 1 vs field.stories.tsx:31-35.
findings.fix: Fix the Playground (or the wiring, see the K2 finding) so the example follows the guidance.

findings.subject: input (AtomTextField), textarea (AtomTextEditor), field (AtomFormField)
findings.summary: iOS fields do not draw the disabled state, though conformance evidence claims it.
findings.evidence: No @Environment(\.isEnabled) in AtomTextField/AtomTextEditor/AtomFormField; AtomFormField.swift:64 forces textPrimary; AtomRendererConformance.swift:73-74,103-104,118-119 list 'disabled' as implemented. The conformance test only compares declared lists (AtomRendererConformanceTests.swift:7-21).
findings.fix: Read isEnabled in AtomFormField and dim title, content and border with AtomTokens.Control.disabledOpacity; add a disabled snapshot.

findings.subject: field (AtomFormField)
findings.summary: AtomFormField hides its title from VoiceOver, so content without its own accessibilityLabel loses its name.
findings.evidence: AtomFormField.swift:45 .accessibilityHidden(true); only AtomTextField/AtomTextEditor add accessibilityLabel(title).
findings.fix: Apply .accessibilityLabel(title) (or accessibilityElement(children: .contain) with the title as label) to styledContent inside AtomFormField.

findings.subject: textarea (AtomTextEditor)
findings.summary: AtomTextEditor's minimum height does not scale with Dynamic Type.
findings.evidence: AtomTextEditor.swift:22,53 minHeight: CGFloat = 112.
findings.fix: Use @ScaledMetric for the default minimum height.

findings.subject: form (AtomFormMessage)
findings.summary: AtomFormMessage is a titled tone callout while web FormMessage is an inline error line: the counterpart has a different anatomy and axes.
findings.evidence: AtomFormMessage.swift:3-52 vs form/form.tsx:136-156.
findings.fix: Decide whether the iOS counterpart of FormMessage is the error line inside AtomFormField (and AtomFormMessage maps to Alert/Notice instead), then record the mapping in a cross-renderer contract.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: Amount without a locale renders differently on server and client, a hydration mismatch.
findings.evidence: amount.tsx:62 new Intl.NumberFormat(locale) with locale undefined; apps/storybook/ssr/ssr.test.tsx only renders to string.
findings.fix: Default locale from UIProvider (or require it in SSR contexts) and add a hydration test.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: A long amount overflows at display size on web, while iOS shrinks it.
findings.evidence: amount.css:23 white-space: nowrap; AtomAmountText.swift:62 minimumScaleFactor(0.5).
findings.fix: Allow the component to shrink (container-query font clamp or max-inline-size with font-size reduction) and add a long-amount story.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: AtomAmountText has no snapshot, and the size axis has different names on the two platforms.
findings.evidence: No amount png under examples/ios-demo/Atom63DemoTests/__Snapshots__/; web size md|lg (amount.tsx:14) vs iOS role .display/.displayLarge (AtomAmountText.swift:29,42).
findings.fix: Add amount to the demo catalog snapshots and add a cross-renderer mapping md->display, lg->displayLarge.

findings.subject: input-otp
findings.summary: OTP slots reverse in right-to-left pages.
findings.evidence: input-otp.tsx:20-25 sets no dir; slots are a flex row (input-otp.css:27-30).
findings.fix: Set dir="ltr" on the OTP container by default (overridable) and add an RTL story.

findings.subject: input-otp
findings.summary: OTP slots have one fixed size and no touch target.
findings.evidence: input-otp.css:40-44.
findings.fix: Covered by the cross-cutting K5 fix; add a lg slot size only if product asks.

findings.subject: autocomplete
findings.summary: Autocomplete tests skip keyboard selection and its popup has no visual baseline.
findings.evidence: autocomplete.test.tsx (4 tests); menu-anatomy png closed.
findings.fix: Add arrow/Enter/Escape tests and open-popup stories.

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: Select popup has no visual baseline.
findings.evidence: ui-react-select-grouped / -scrollable pngs show the closed trigger.
findings.fix: Open the popup in those stories.

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: The select popup's visual quality cannot be judged: no baseline shows it.
findings.evidence: Same screenshots as above.
findings.fix: Capture the popup in 4 themes x 2 modes for YZ's contact sheet.

findings.subject: input (AtomTextField)
findings.summary: AtomTextField placeholder colour and error hint differ from web: textSecondary vs text-tertiary, and a hard-coded English 'Error: ' prefix.
findings.evidence: AtomTextField.swift:62,68; AtomFormField.swift:53; input.css:90.
findings.fix: Use textTertiary for prompts and a localized string for the error prefix.

findings.subject: input
findings.summary: No forced-colors rule: invalid and default field borders become the same system colour.
findings.evidence: grep forced-colors in input.css/textarea.css/input-otp.css finds nothing.
findings.fix: In forced colors, thicken the invalid border or add an outline so invalid stays distinguishable.

findings.subject: input
findings.summary: InputGroupTextarea ignores the group's size.
findings.evidence: input-group.tsx:169-182 reads disabled/invalid but not size from context.
findings.fix: Pass size from InputGroupContext.

findings.subject: form
findings.summary: FormControl points aria-describedby at a description id that may not exist, and FormMessage combines role=alert with aria-live=polite.
findings.fix: Register FormDescription presence in context before referencing its id; drop aria-live (role=alert is implicit assertive) or use role=status.

findings.subject: input-otp
findings.summary: InputOTP has no invalid prop while Input and Textarea do, and the caret uses text-primary as a background (craft-baseline token-role entry).
findings.evidence: input-otp.tsx:12-27; craft-baseline.json 'token-role | .../input-otp.css | background-color: var(--a63-text-primary)' (input-otp.css:104).
findings.fix: Add invalid (sets aria-invalid on the hidden input) and paint the caret with currentColor, then drop the baseline entry.

findings.subject: textarea
findings.summary: Textarea has no variant axis while Input and SearchField have default/filled/plain.
findings.evidence: textarea.json lists no variants; input.json variants.
findings.fix: Decide whether filled/plain apply to multiline fields; add them to textarea.json if so.

findings.subject: label
findings.summary: Label has a single font size, so it stays md beside sm or lg fields.
findings.evidence: label.css:14.
findings.fix: Inherit the size from Field or add a size prop mapped to the control ramp.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: An invalid currency code throws during render.
findings.evidence: amount.tsx:62.
findings.fix: Catch the RangeError and fall back to a plain number with a dev warning.
